rationale: This is essentially cash-based operating profitability (Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev 2016) crossed with the Sloan accrual anomaly, and the binary INDICATOR collapses every gate-failing firm to exactly zero, so the bottom of the cross-section conflates "high-profit but accrual-heavy" with "unprofitable," destroying the ranking's economic ordering.

The MIN bottleneck of a five-period downside profitability floor and low leverage is internally consistent and the sign is right, though both legs are individually well-mined (profitability and leverage/distress) so the incremental content rests entirely on the TS_MIN "durability" twist rather than a genuinely new mechanism.

The two legs are near-mechanical duplicates — the change in retained earnings *is* net income less dividends, so TREND(re/at) is largely a smoothed restatement of the profitability leg it multiplies, making this a redundant self-interaction rather than a cross-theme conditioning signal.

A coherent DuPont-flavored composite (margin conditioned on turnover stability) with a correctly signed, non-degenerate construction, but the fundamental-volatility leg overlaps heavily with documented earnings-stability/low-risk effects, so novelty is moderate rather than high.

This is not a cross-theme interaction at all but a single rescaled profitability ratio — oiadp/lt is mechanically ROA times an inverse-leverage factor — making it a trivial denominator swap on the standard profitability anomaly with added small-denominator instability for near-debt-free firms.

The expression, hypothesis, and negative expected sign are mutually consistent and the multiplicative form genuinely targets a joint fragility state, but the resulting construct is a close proxy for the published financial-distress anomaly, so it should be judged on whether it beats a simple leverage or earnings-volatility baseline.
